messages.subject: drop2 not working with facet_items=F
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

Any idea why the drop2 option (both default and explicit drop2=T) are ignored when facet_items=F ?

The following code demonstrates how it's impossible to get all ICC curves on one plot and avoid plotting the downward P(Y=0) curves too.

ThreePL_fit <- mirt(SAPA, model="F = 1-16", itemtype="3PL", SE=T)
plot(ThreePL_fit, type='trace')
plot(ThreePL_fit, type='trace', drop2=T, facet_items=F)

Thanks,

-Henry

messages.subject: Item difficulty parameters (Rasch) not centering at 0?
messages.subject_clean: Item difficulty parameters (Rasch) not centering at 0?
messages.body_plain:
Hey all!

I've only been using mirt a couple years. I just got hired onto a job where Winsteps is used to get item difficulty parameters. I compared my mirt results with their results, and noticed a shift in parameter estimates.

I checked the MEAN_1 by adding the argument pars = "values" and it was set to 0. In order to adjust my parameters so they were centered around 0 I had to adjust MEAN_1 upward. For example, if my average item difficulty was -1.7, then I had to enter MEAN_1 = 1.7. This resulted in an average item difficulty of 0.

I checked this on two other data sets (ayala form mirt, and one data set included in the ministep program called bond4). Similar results.

I've tried to include a folder of my r script, the data sets, and control files for winsteps (though running Winsteps is not needed because I include the results in a spreadsheet).

Perhaps there is a simple answer/solution that I missed. Otherwise I would have put this on the mirt-issues page on Github.

Any thoughts?

Grateful for all your hard work!

messages.subject: How to interpret LD standardised residuals
messages.subject_clean: How to interpret LD standardised residuals
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

In examining the local independence assumption recent updates of mirt  provide standardisation of the residuals.  I am wondering how to interpret these residuals.  If I am not wrong one way is to search for values above 1.96 or 2.57. However, in his article Toland (2014) using the IRTPRO suggests that residuals with absolute values above |10| denote violation of the assumption. What is your opinion?

Best regards,

Nikos

messages.subject: Formula for calculating item information from graded response model
messages.subject_clean: Formula for calculating item information from graded response model
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

       Thank you for the very useful mirt package.

        Recently, I tried applying a graded response model to an ordinal scale with four response options. When I compared the item characteristic curves for a graded response model from mirt (EM algorithm) and MPLUS (WLSMV estimator), they looked essentially the same (mirt output left, mplus output right).

      However, when looking at the corresponding item information curves, the shapes remained very similar, but the magnitudes of total information were different.

       Would you happen to know the formula used in mirt to calculate the item information in the graded response model? I was thinking the formula might help me  figure out the reason for the differences in item information. Sorry if my question is naive.

         Thank you for your time,
         Raymond

messages.subject: Re: Formula for calculating item information from graded response model
messages.subject_clean: Formula for calculating item information from graded response model
messages.body_plain:
It might have something to do with how Mplus scales the latent traits, which would also factor into the calculation of the y-axis. mirt assumes the latent trait is scaled 0-1, though Mplus often prefers indicator codings to allow the variance of the latent traits to be estimated while fixing a slope coefficient to 1. Otherwise, I'm not quite sure why Mplus would be different  in terms of the reported magnitudes.

Phil

     Thanks again for your responses, and for the very helpful mirt package.

      Best,
      Raymond
